title: Tis The (Earnings) Season
description: Updates on the High Conviction Trade Series, and What I'm Looking For Next
body_html:
Disclaimer: By reading this article, you acknowledge and agree to the terms and conditions

It’s been a busy start to earnings season. Five out of six names covered in previous articles reported excellent results, and more are set to report this week. I wanted to briefly discuss each report, some recent events (Argentina Elections and a Potential China Trade deal), and the setups I find most attractive.

At the time of writing (Sunday 7:39 PM), preliminary results indicate Javier Milei’s party, La Libertad Avanza, is headed towards a decisive victory.

I’m long a small basket of Argentinian Financial Institutions, all of whom were trashed this year over fears that Milei’s pivot to Free Markets would be overturned at the ballot box. Grupo Galicia, Banco Macro, and Banco BBVA Argentina have heavily underperformed the MSCI Argentina, and if Milei’s party indeed secures 40%+ of the vote I think the combination of US Support (via a $20 Billion Swap Line to support Argentina’s currency) and political certainty for the next two years will provide an excellent backdrop for these banks to recover much of their 2025 YTD losses.

I certainly don’t expect them to bounce back to 0% YTD within a day, but the names should be up 15%+ given the lethal bear case is now entirely removed. The reaction today is likely to be “kneejerk”, so if you are interested in Argentinian banks, I think it make sense to wait and see how things settle out this week.

Nonetheless, I think the “Argentina Comeback” trade is one that will last for a while given Milei’s free market reforms, and that regardless of today’s knee-jerk move, the positive trend among Argentinian financials, energy (YPF), and airports (CAAP), will continue for some time.

It also seems a “Sweetheart” trade truce between the US and China is on track. Both sides are already drawing attention to the meeting and praising the “tough but understandable stance” of the other negotiators, so that they can both play off an agreement as a win. Will anything of substance happen? Probably not, but mere reassurance is enough to get markets happy again.

Most names within the “Tariff Slime” basket have already recovered from the April 4th lows, but I think increased trade certainty could benefit names heavily associated with product sourcing from China and Southeast Asia such as Gigacloud Technology, Sonos, and Jakks Pacific, as well as tech names such as ACM Research (semiconductor cleaning equipment) given the prospect of a chip-war detente.

Between Argentinian Banks and “Tariff Slime”, I think Argentinian assets provide a more favorable long term setup, but given the event-driven nature of today’s market and a massive fixation on “themes”, I think both groups are worth paying attention to today.

Earnings Analysis and Setups

1. Customer’s Bancorp

Multiples: 8.9x 2026 EPS, 1.17x Tangible Book Value

Reported: $2.20 vs $1.90 Estimate

Takeaway: Strong Beat and Guidance Upgrade Boosts 2026 Outlook

Customer’s delivered a significant beat. The quarter was marked by excellent credit quality, accelerating loan growth, and increasing deposit activity driven by its newly hired banking teams.

The regional bank industry has been plagued by credit “cockroaches”, which makes Customer’s beat even more impressive. Customer’s dispelled any concern over its sizeable NDFI (Non Depository Financial Institution) loan book, stating:

Most of the recent attention this past quarter has been on the lender finance space. For Customers, this is one of the oldest specialized lending businesses we’ve been in. It’s one we’ve been in for over a decade, and we’ve not only had zero losses, but zero loan defaults. In this business, this is typically lending to a private credit fund where the collateral is a broadly diversifies pool of loans out to middle market companies. There’s significant overcollateralization. We have low advance rates and there is a -- it’s very diversified. So our single obligor exposure is very low, kind of mid single-digit. So when you put all those things together, it’s translated into, again, zero losses, zero defaults.

Customer’s also highlighted the success of its proprietary CUBIX offering. CUBIX is a private payments rail (similar to Zelle, but for Insitutions) that allows clients to transfer hundreds of Billions to other Customer’s clients. The primary use case for this is Institutional crypto activity. CUBIX is integrated across all major exchanges and most trading desks, and comes with an added element of security relative to pure stablecoins like USDC or Tether, since CUBIX can only be transferred to other Institutional CUBIX clients, and thus can’t really be stolen or hacked by third parties.

Customer’s has brought in nearly $3.9 Billion in zero-cost deposits (which they store in cash to minimize liquidity risk) via CUBIX, and growth has been accelerating as crypto trading volume hits record highs.

Customer’s provided very rosy guidance in terms of organic deposit growth, stating that its new 2025 hires are likely to give a “25% lift on the $300 - $400 Million” in quarterly deposit growth, starting in the middle of next year.

What I like about Customer’s is that time is on its side and that its successes build upon each other. Unlike other regionals stuck with low-rate securities or deteriorating office loans, Customer’s winning technology solutions such as CUBIX, and its highly successful new banking teams (poached from Flagstar, Signature, and SVB) contribute to the bottom line immediately and help it secure new opportunities and clients. Simply put, it’s a growth story, not a value story.

Despite Customer’s history of success and its impressive 46% YTD return, it still trades at a steep discount to the broader regional banking index (9x 2026 EPS, 1.17x Tangible Book Value vs 10x 2026 EPS, 1.47x Tangible Book Value for the index). Customer’s has differentiated itself from peers via its proprietary offerings such as CUBIX, its minimal credit risk, and its consistent growth track record, and as analysts slowly bump 2026 estimates up from $7.50 to $8.00 and as investors warm to the name, I think additional upside is present. A baseline case would be for it to trade at the Regional Bank peer multiple (implying $80 a share) and an optimistic case would be for it to trade at 11-12x earnings (implying $88 - $96 a share).

2. SE Holdings and Incubations (9478 JP Equity)

Multiples: 3.8x 2025 EPS, 0.59x Tangible Book Value

Reported: 6 Yen - Adjusted 57 Yen

Takeaway: A Record Quarter, Real Estate Divestment, and a Fresh Buyback Provides a Springboard to an ATH

SE Holdings and Incubations reported a record quarter, with Net Asset Value per share increasing 10% from 571 Yen to 630 Yen, driven by a buoyant stock market.

While SE Holdings appears as a publisher on first glance, its real gem is its massive Securities Portfolio, which generates sizeable dividends and interest income that the company utilizes to repurchase shares at a massive discount to Net Asset Value.

After reporting results last week, the company announced a fresh 150 Million Yen repurchase program over the weekend. The repurchase will run from October 27th to November 28th. The company also announced the sale of real estate property which will close in early 2026. The message SE Holdings is sending couldn’t be more clear: they want to close the discount to NAV.

As long term shareholders we want the price to stay flat during the repurchase, or better yet, go down!

The company is about to repurchase 4% of the float over the next 4 weeks, at 66% upside to Net Asset Value. The cheaper they can repurchase these shares, the more beneficial it is to us. Given that on quiet days 9478 trades just 30,000 shares a day, a 375,000 share buyback is a challenging task.

9478 is one of my highest conviction trades this year, and I think the setup is great long term. It has excellent capital allocation, and treats shareholders like partners rather than adversaries (as is the case in most cheap Japanese value setups). I think it may one day trade as high as 0.75x Net Asset Value (which would imply 472 Yen), but if you are considering adding to your position I think it makes sense to be less aggressive over the next four weeks, and to let the company complete its repurchase program at favorable prices.

3. Bank of the Ryukyus (8399 JP Equity)

Multiples: 7.8x 2026 EPS, 0.46x Tangible Book Value

Reported: 61 Yen

Takeaway: Rising Japanese Interest Rates Drive Record Results, Dividend Hike and Guidance Boost to Fuel Next Leg Higher

Bank of the Ryukyu’s delivered a record breaking quarter, and significantly upgraded guidance along with a dividend increase from 40 Yen to 54 Yen.

While I am growing less bullish on the Japanese Banking Industry as a whole, and recently sold my position in industry giants like MUFG, I think smaller banks that are highly sensitive to rising rates, such as Bank of the Ryukyus (8399), Mebuki Financial (7167), and Juroku Financial Group (7380), are still compelling setups.

All of these names trade at a steep discount to their own Tangible Book Values, and 2-3x turns cheaper than peers. I think as long as the beat-and-raise and dividends hikes continue, they’re decent holds in the 8-9x Earnings range.

4. OP Bancorp (OPBK US Equity)

Multiples: 6.8x 2026 EPS, 0.92x Tangible Book Value

Reported: $0.45 vs $0.44 Estimate

Takeaway: Strong Beat, Rates Down to Drive Record 2026 Results

OP Bancorp reported its highest quarterly earnings since early 2023, and is well on-track for $2.00 in 2026.

Credit quality remained strong, and its Net Interest Margin improved to 3.26%. OP Bancorp has an extremely high cost of deposits (4.06%) since it operates in the highly competitive “Ethnic” Los Angeles market. While some may consider this a long-term liability, in a rates down environment OP has significant room for improvement.

With just $600 Million in variable rate loans and $1.7 Billion in high cost deposits, OP Bancorp is well positioned to take advantage of dovish monetary policy. Now that OP is a Russell 2000 component, I think increased institutional attention, high insider ownership (20%), a respectable dividend yield (3.4%), and pure play exposure to “rates down” make the shares compelling at just 6.8x 2026 Earnings. I have been adding to my position and think that OP has upside to tangible book value of $14.88 a share.

5. Waterstone Financial (WSBF US Equity)

Multiples: 8.5x 2026 EPS, 0.82x Tangible Book Value

Reported: $0.45

Takeaway: Momentum Continues, Lower Mortgage Rates to Provide Earnings Infusion

Waterstone reported $0.90 for the six months ended September 30th, its strongest showing since 2021. Net Interest Income rose 7.5% in the quarter, driven by loan growth and rapidly decreasing deposit costs.

Waterstone has a sizeable mortgage origination division, which swung back into profitability earlier this year. With mortgage rates plummeting to their lowest since 2022, Waterstone is poised for a strong Q4.

What I like about Waterstone is you are getting the “right-tail” optionality of the mortgage origination business (which generates significant fee-income) at an attractive regional banking multiple. Waterstone trades at a steep discount to Tangible Book Value of $18.65 a share, and is actively addressing the discount via its share repurchase program (the company repurchase 270,000 shares at an average price of $14.15 a share in Q3).

With mortgage rates primed for further declines, I think Waterstone is simply too cheap to ignore at 8.5x 2026 Earnings and 18% below its Tangible Book Value. The company earned nearly $0.75 a quarter in the 2021 mortgage refinancing wave - while I don’t think $0.75 a quarter is within reach next year, I certainly think the company could hit $0.55 - $0.65, which would put the stock at an even lower 6.3x multiple. With share repurchases in the low 14’s likely to support the stock, I think the shares are attractive in the low $15s and provide an excellent way to gain exposure to the mortgage optionality of the RKT’s PFS’s and UWMC’s of the world, at a low multiple. In an ideal world, I think Waterstone trades in the $16 to $18 range, but given the company is repurchasing 2% of shares a quarter at the current levels I’m happy if it stays where it is for now.

6. Kearny Financial (KRNY US Equity)

Multiples: 8.6x 2026 EPS, 0.67x Tangible Book Value

Reported: $0.15 vs $0.16 Estimate

Takeaway: Steady Progress, Rate Cuts Provide Clear Path to $0.21 a Quarter

Kearny was the only name of the six to “miss” results. $0.15 was a significant improvement from last quarter, and Kearny is well on its way to get back to $0.21 a quarter early next year (provided we get a further two rate cuts).

Non-performing assets spiked from $45.6 Million to $64.6 Million, primarily due to one construction loan that is currently under contract for sale (and thus likely to be repaid with no credit loss).

Kearny’s Net Interest Margin grew from 2.00% to 2.10% during the quarter, and stands to benefit from rising loan yields as CRE loans reprice higher in late 2026 and early 2027.

Kearny is historically a poor performer relative to Customer’s, Waterstone, and OP Bancorp, but I think its steep discount to book and large room for improvement in 2026 and 2027 create an attractive setup. The 6.7% dividend is unlikely to be reduced, and ultimately I think Kearny has upside to the mid 7s as rate cuts continue to boost earnings.

Discussion

While all of these trades are favorites of mine, you can have favorites among favorites. Customers Bancorp (CUBI) and SE Holdings (9478) remain high conviction trades and I think they possess the most upside. Customers is a growth name trading at a value multiple (relative to markets and closely comparable peers) and continues to impress. Coverage has increased, and a favorable regulatory backdrop has shifted CUBIX from being considered a liability to a growth asset. I think SE Holdings sizeable discount to Tangible Book, paired with its share repurchase program creates an attractive short and long-term setup. The sale of its real estate garners immediate attention from Japanese microcap investors who look for hints of shifting capital alloaction, and its rapid fire share repurchases mint a perfect value investor setup - it’s not hard to see how a position in a name at 4x adjusted earnings and 0.59x Tangible Book, paired with a 10% yearly repurchase program, can go right.

Looking ahead, Oppenheimer (OPY US Equity), Capital Georgia (CGEO LN Equity), and Itafos (IFOS CN Equity) are set to report later this week.

Oppenheimer faces a near term headwind due to the rise in its stock price, which is closely tied to variable employee compensation expenses, but the favorable backdrop for Capital Markets and Wealth Management should drive earnings to the highest since 2021. At less than 9x trailing earnings and likely around 8x forward earnings, I think it is ridiculously cheap for an investment bank with high “right-tail” potential when Capital Markets activity surges.

Capital Georgia is likely to report record Net Asset Value and positive marks across its Georgian Private Equity Portfolio, the main thing I will be paying attention to, however, is whether it intends to continue share repurchases at the currently $75 Million USD a year rate. With NAV likely to be in the 3400 GBP - 3500 GBP range, I think the stock has additional upside to 0.8x Tangible Book Value, which would imply 2,700 GBP a share.

Itafos is likely sitting on its largest Net Cash position in history, especially after the liquidation of its stake in St George’s Mining (SGQ AU Equity). The earnings estimate of $0.12 CAD is standalone impressive (given Itafos specializes in Phosphate based fertilizer which is primarily dominated by China, thus making it a “strategic” asset), but I will be paying special attention to the Capital Allocation outlook. Itafos is no longer struggling, and I am curious to see what their plans are for their new cash war chest. Earlier this year, they paid their first dividend in years, I think the announcement of a regular dividend or share repurchase would garner significant interest in the stock.

Lastly, I have been adding slightly to my CBL Associates (CBL US Equity) position. CBL faces a near-term headwind as Taconic Capital Advisors winds down and liquidates its 595,300 share position, which I think may have caused some of the $31 to $29.50 move. In more positive news, CBL continues to announce attractive refinancings, asset dispositions, and its Term Loan is trading at the highest in history, 97 cents on the dollar.

The rise in the Term Loan encourages me. CBL is largely a balance-sheet story, if lenders are willing to refinance individual properties at lower rates and the term loan continues to trade upwards towards 100, it not only contributes directly to the bottom line (via lower interest expense), it initiates a positive spiral where people become more comfortable with CBL credit. Given CBL trades at just 4.3x Funds From Operation, I think the debt market’s confidence in CBL is highly beneficial to equity holders.

Looking ahead, I think Oppenheimer has the best chance of “wowing” investors. Everyone is already factoring in high compensation expenses due to appreciation in the stock price, so if they indeed come in higher than $1.00 it will be a very nice surprise. Investment Banking and Wealth Management is a much more prestigious sector than Real Estate or Industrials, and with pure Investment Banks and Brokerages trading at record highs, a strong result out of Oppenheimer is all that is needed to attract attention and initiate a re-rate to 10-12x earnings (which would imply $75- $90 a share).

We had an excellent start to earnings season, and I’m hopeful the positive momentum continues. With panic over credit “cockroaches” and trade and inflation fears alleviating, I think “rates down” names such as Waterstone, OP Bancorp, and Kearny, as well as “growth” names such as Customers, SE Holdings, Oppenheimer, and Capital Georgia, are worth considering, especially if you want to supplement a tech-heavy or large-cap heavy portfolio with value names at 7-9x earnings. I’ll be monitoring these names closely and will provide further updates once results are out.
